summary: LUNA-VIEW is a lunar south-pole mission geometry explorer that helps teams examine when the Sun and Earth are visible from a selected surface coordinate. Users can choose a location and UTC period, inspect source-backed Sun and Earth azimuth and elevation, compare two sites, explore 24-hour or 30-day timelines, and download CSV or PDF reports. The application queries NASA/JPL Horizons through a constrained FastAPI service and clearly labels live, cached, partial, and unavailable results. It never replaces failed scientific requests with simulated values. Optional LOLA-derived horizon profiles can add terrain obstruction when verified data are configured. LUNA-VIEW supports early exploration and education while clearly separating geometric visibility from power, radio-link, and landing-safety claims.
details:
LUNA-VIEW turns a lunar latitude, east longitude, altitude, and UTC time range into an interactive view of apparent Sun and Earth geometry. The React interface displays horizon views, sampled visibility lanes, continuous illumination and Earth-visibility windows, site comparisons, scientific status, and downloadable reports. A FastAPI backend validates every request, applies range and sample limits, and makes server-controlled observer queries to NASA/JPL Horizons for the Sun and Earth. The browser cannot construct arbitrary upstream queries.

The project addresses a practical early-planning question: how do illumination and geometric Earth visibility change with location and time near the lunar south pole? This matters because polar lighting changes sharply with geometry, while a clear view of Earth affects direct-communication opportunities. LUNA-VIEW makes these patterns easier to explore without presenting them as final engineering results.

The application uses React, TypeScript, Vite, SVG, FastAPI, Pydantic, HTTPX, Uvicorn, jsPDF, Nginx, and Docker Compose. Automated frontend and backend tests cover calculations, validation, parsing, failure behavior, and report generation. The interface exposes provenance, retrieval timestamps, coordinate conventions, and data completeness. When no verified LOLA horizon profile matches a coordinate, terrain is explicitly marked unavailable rather than estimated.

The design prioritizes scientific honesty. Solar visibility does not estimate electrical power. Earth visibility does not calculate an RF link budget. Preset coordinates are illustrative and do not represent approved landing sites. The application is an educational and early exploration aid, not certified flight software or a NASA-endorsed product.
